h: Plan your visit and explore the bay
p: The aquarium is a perfect fit for a seaside day in Newquay because it doesn't need to take up the whole day. A couple of hours inside is plenty for most families, and you're right on the beach as soon as you step out. That makes it ideal for those moments when the weather turns, the kids need a change of scene or everyone just fancies a break from the sand.

Time your visit around the talks if you can. Find out what's on when you arrive and plan your route through the displays so you're in the right place at the right time. The keepers are a mine of information, and children love asking questions about the sharks and turtles.

Tips: Newquay gets very busy in the school summer holidays, so visiting earlier in the day can help you avoid the crowds. If you're driving, parking around the town centre can fill up quickly at peak times, so give yourself a bit of extra time.

There's plenty more to enjoy nearby. Newquay Zoo, set in Trenance Gardens, is a lovely add-on for animal lovers, with a boating lake and leisure area alongside. Up on the headland, the little white Huer's Hut is a historic lookout where someone once watched for shoals of pilchards and called the fishing boats out.
Then, of course, there are the beaches. Towan, Great Western and Tolcarne are all close to the town centre, while Fistral is the place to watch the surfers or book a lesson of your own.
